title: MLV Studio — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Slide Atlas. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Slide Atlas
options.lineage: Brightfield histology, Cajal's camera-lucida drawings, the comparison microscope
options.thesis: Every drawing is a specimen on a lit stage, stained by the property you measure.
options.viewport: Slide-box rail of numbered slots; the active drawing on a brightfield stage with vernier x/y rulers, objective-turret zoom and stain chips; a frosted-label inspector at right.
options.risk: The microscope can turn into costume unless every part (box, label, stage, stain, turret) does real work.

raised.raise: Colour quarantine: chrome is neutral glass and enamel; every chroma on screen is a stain, i.e. data, with legend and units.
Two type sizes in the chrome; rank is carried by weight, case and rule.
Focus mode: one slide owns the viewport, the next pre-rendered one keystroke away.
Nothing disappears: subsets and splits void and cross-reference on the label instead of deleting.

options.label: Calibrated Grey Field
options.lineage: The psychophysics display: mean-luminance grey, fixation cross, gamma ramp
options.thesis: The tool is the experiment screen: a calibrated grey field where the white stimulus is the only bright thing.
options.viewport: A white stimulus window floating in mid-grey; controls recede into grey-on-grey rails; the fixation cross is the cursor.
options.risk: The most familiar world to this audience; grey-on-grey chrome can feel flat over long sessions.

options.label: Dark-first Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels with hairline seams; the white stimulus is the one lit pane.
options.viewport: Tiled persistent panels: library, canvas, inspector, console-like provenance log.
options.case: Holds product clarity and matches R/IDE habits; weaker audience identification than the slide atlas.
options.risk: Close to the category default for science tools.

options.label: Parameter Specimen
options.thesis: One giant drawing; drag a parameter and a grid of every drawing re-measures live.
options.viewport: A single drawing at enormous scale over a breathing grid of the batch, sliders as the only chrome.
options.case: Strong clarity for parameter scrubbing (trace, split); its audience is type designers, not vision scientists.
options.risk: Thin for dense inspection: tables and MAT layers have no home.

options.label: Atlas Plate
options.thesis: Black text columns; drawings appear as bordered colour plates, the only colour in the system.
options.viewport: A text column of measurements faces a bordered plate of the stained drawing; guide words name the range in view.
options.case: Holds audience for teaching and figures; weaker for interactive inspection.
options.risk: Reads as a book, not an instrument.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One drawing per screen, flick to the next.
options.viewport: One stimulus fills the viewport; action glyphs stacked right.
options.case: Loses both axes: no audience fit, no room for measurement.
options.kept: Focus mode with the next item pre-rendered.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each operation a coupon that stamps used or void.
options.viewport: Operations as torn-off coupons in a wallet.
options.case: Loses both axes: travel ephemera has nothing to do with vision science.
options.kept: Nothing disappears; it cancels and stays traceable.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: Pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and rule.
options.viewport: A raked rack of tinted slides.
options.case: Loses both axes: the raked tinting would distort stimuli.
options.risk: Geometry distortion is disqualifying for a measurement tool.
options.kept: Rank by weight, case and rule, not size.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A napari/Fiji-style scientific viewer, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Tool palette left, layer list right, dark viewer centre with the drawing.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every image-analysis tool by design.
